findings.title: git -c / --config-env with an exec-capable key (and the GIT_* exec environment variables) pass check_git on non-push subcommands although the gate's own GIT_EXEC_CONFIG names those keys as command-running
findings.body: gates.py defines GIT_EXEC_CONFIG (core.pager, core.editor, core.sshcommand, core.hookspath, sequence.editor, diff.external, pager.*, alias.*, remote.*.uploadpack/receivepack, ...) and applies it only to `git config <key> <value>` writes and to `git clone -c/--config`. parse_git_globals collects `-c key=value` and `--config-env key=VAR` into `cfg`, but check_git only inspects `cfg` for `alias.*`; git_exec_route(sub, args) receives the post-subcommand args and never sees `cfg`. So a single plain command such as `git -c core.pager='git push origin main' log` is allowed: route_mentions sees no `git push` token (the value is one token, basename != git; RISKY is applied only to sh/eval wrappers), readonly_invocation treats `log` as read-only, and check_git finds no alias key. The same holds for `git -c core.sshCommand=... fetch origin`, `git -c sequence.editor=... rebase -i`, `git -c core.hooksPath=<dir> commit`, and for the environment forms the design already acknowledges for retargeting (GIT_RETARGET covers GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_COMMON_DIR only): `GIT_PAGER=... git log`, `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=... git rebase -i`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=... git fetch`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file> git <any>`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n`. These are documented, non-disguised single-command forms, and the gate already classifies the config-key equivalents as routes, so the allowlist is not closed on its own terms. Fix: in check_git deny when any key in `cfg` (from -c or --config-env) matches GIT_EXEC_CONFIG (the bundle prompt states `git -c` is denied by design, which today only holds when a push/alias is present); extend GIT_RETARGET-style denial to GIT_PAGER, GIT_EDITOR, GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR, GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_ASKPASS, GIT_PROXY_COMMAND, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (assignment tokens and `env` forms, as done for MAENG_*); and have route_mentions apply RISKY to env-assignment and `-c` values so a push hidden in such a value makes the command non-canonical. Pin each with a deny test in R1b.

findings.title: needs-external-check: installed gh subcommand inventory and installed git exec-capable options (tool_reference is null)
findings.body: The bundle was built with --no-tool-ref, so tool_reference is null and every option/subcommand-semantics judgment below could not be checked against the installed binaries and is reported here instead of guessed. (1) gh: GH_ALLOWED makes the `issue` group fully open (every action except `delete` is a write needing -R). Against the installed gh help, confirm the current `gh issue` action list and that none of them publishes repository content or refs beyond issue metadata; in particular `gh issue develop` creates a remote branch (and with --checkout a local one) and `gh issue transfer` moves across repositories, both classified as plain `write` today (no G3 destination check for --checkout, no verification of the created ref). Also confirm `gh pr edit` has no flag that merges or changes the head ref, that `gh pr close --delete-branch` is the only ref-deleting flag in the allowed pr actions, and that `gh browse`, `gh status`, `gh search` and `gh completion` remain read-only with every flag. (2) git: GIT_EXEC_OPTIONS lists exec-capable options per subcommand (rebase --exec/-x, difftool --extcmd/--tool, mergetool --tool, grep -O, fetch/pull/clone/ls-remote --upload-pack, archive --exec, send-email *-cmd). Against the installed `git <sub> -h` for every GIT_BUILTINS entry allowed as mutating in a personal directory, confirm no other option runs a caller-supplied command (candidates to check: `git log/diff/show --ext-diff`, `git am --interactive`/`--patch-format` hooks, `git notes edit`, `git clone/init --template=<dir>`, `git push --receive-pack`/`--exec` (currently denied because parse_canonical_push rejects every unlisted flag, so this one does not depend on help), `git worktree add` hooks, `git maintenance start` which installs launchd/cron jobs). (3) readonly.py GIT_LONG/GIT_LONG_VALUE and the gh GH_READ_FLAGS sets: confirm no listed option writes a file or opens a pager/editor on the installed versions (e.g. `--output` is handled for git; `--web`/`-w` opens a browser only). Until these are checked against the installed git/gh, the closedness claims for the gh issue group and for the git exec-option table rest on memory, not on tool_reference.

findings.body: Resolved at head c3eede5 (tree 8ffb2609): the round-9 high finding (S2 failing three checks) is cleared by the attached fresh, run-id-checked run e2644258 (finished 2026-10-17T18:24:30): S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S7, S8, S9 and GF1-GF3 all PASS; the only FAIL rows are exactly the four dispositioned ones (S5 agent/loose-skill leak -> MAE-224; GF4 malformed exit-0 hook output -> host limit). The round-9 R1b medium (submodule foreach, rebase --exec, bisect run, filter-branch, difftool --extcmd) is closed in core code by GIT_EXEC_OPTIONS/GIT_EXEC_ACTIONS/GIT_EXEC_SUBS/git_exec_route (unambiguous long-option prefixes and short-option clusters handled); the round-9 low on file-tool writes into MAENG_HOME is closed by harness_state_root in g3_edit plus state_taint and the redirect check for Bash. The remaining round-9 lows concern test pins in delegated files (tests/) and are for the R1b review. AC-1..AC-3: runner evidence seq 141-147 at tree 8ffb2609 equals the head tree (evidence_binding shows no differing paths) and the ev-exec-R1.txt output shas (1eb8a0de9f68, 0ef67f7b440f, c543a9b0eec1, fca391796184 for 471 tests OK, 8172ceeb2b08, 25da1db8bc90, 6d6c442f8589) match the recorded output_sha256 prefixes. AC-5: S4.models.json ok=true with haiku/opus/sonnet resolved per agent and no write tool used by researcher/architect. AC-6: S5 shows maeng-harness absent, zero maeng hook output, eta unchanged. Residual (not blocking): the staging run itself is a declared check (seq 148) and the per-scenario summaries are excluded from the bundle, so the fact that the smoke ran against the head code (commit message says 61bbeed, which differs from head only by tests/live/evidence/**, a non-code glob) is taken from the commit message rather than verified here; the run.json finished_at (18:24:30) preceding the runner records at the head tree (18:24:34 onward) is consistent with that account.
